## Cross-country term-premium and neutral-rate differentials

Two monthly panels accompany *Model-Free Cross-Country Term Premia*. The first
carries the recovered sovereign term-premium differentials, and the second the
neutral-rate differentials, meaning the part of the government yield differential
that does not contain term premia. Both are measured against the United States,
at every tenor and for every country the paper analyses, so that a differential
of one is the complement of the other within the same government yield
differential.

| File | Contents | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| [Term-premium differentials (CSV)](files/data/gov_term_premium_differentials_monthly.csv) | 45 series, `dtp_gov_USD_{currency}_{tenor}_bp` | monthly, January 2000 to June 2026 |
| [Neutral-rate differentials (CSV)](files/data/neutral_rate_differentials_monthly.csv) | 45 series, `ndr_USD_{currency}_{tenor}_bp` | monthly, January 2000 to June 2026 |

Each file holds a `Date` column of month-end dates followed by one column per
currency and tenor. The nine partner currencies are the euro, the yen, sterling,
the Swiss franc, the Canadian dollar, the Australian dollar, the New Zealand
dollar, the Swedish krona and the Norwegian krone, and the five tenors are one,
two, five, ten and twenty years. Values are in basis points and empty cells are
months in which a series is not quoted.

## How to read the sign

Every differential is partner minus United States, so that a positive ten-year
value against Germany means the German term premium exceeded the U.S. term
premium in that month. On the released series, ten-year U.S. Treasury term
premia sat 28 basis points below German and 37 basis points below Japanese term
premia over 2002 to 2007, and 56 and 83 basis points above them from 2013
onwards.

## What the series are, and what they are not

The term-premium differentials are recovered from two traded prices, the
long-tenor cross-currency basis and the swap-spread differential, with no
expectations model estimated in any country. The neutral-rate differentials are
the residual of the same identity, the government yield differential less the
recovered term-premium differential, so the two panels sum back to the
government yield differential wherever both are observed.

The series released here are the benchmark-consistent construction on which
every number in the paper rests. The panel opens in January 2000, and the
paper's estimation sample begins in 2002, so the first two years are provided
for completeness rather than used in the paper. The underlying Bloomberg basis,
zero-coupon curve and bid-ask quotes are licensed and cannot be redistributed;
the replication materials therefore carry a checksum manifest of the raw inputs,
sufficient to verify that a rebuild used the same sources.
